entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: 1Sa 5:1, 2 . The Philistines Bring the Ark into the House of Dagon.

entries.heading: 2. the house of Dagon
entries.text: 2. the house of Dagon --Stately temples were erected in honor of this idol, which was the principal deity of the Philistines, but whose worship extended over all Syria, as well as Mesopotamia and Chaldea; its name being found among the Assyrian gods on the cuneiform inscriptions [Rawlinson]. It was represented under a monstrous combination of a human head, breast, and arms, joined to the belly and tail of a fish. The captured ark was placed in the temple of Dagon, right before this image of the idol.

entries.heading: 5. Therefore neither the priests . . . nor any . . . tread on the threshold of Dagon
entries.text: 5. Therefore neither the priests . . . nor any . . . tread on the threshold of Dagon --A superstitious ceremony crept in, and in the providence of God was continued, by which the Philistines contributed to publish this proof of the helplessness of their god. unto this day --The usage continued in practice at the time when this history was written--probably in the later years of Samuel's life.

entries.heading: Verse 6
entries.text: 1Sa 5:6-12 . The Philistines Are Smitten with Emerods.

entries.heading: 7. the ark of God shall not abide with us
entries.text: 7. the ark of God shall not abide with us --It was removed successively to several of the large towns of the country, but the same pestilence broke out in every place and raged so fiercely and fatally that the authorities were forced to send the ark back into the land of Israel [ 1Sa 5:8-10 ].

entries.heading: 11. they sent
entries.text: 11. they sent --that is, the magistrates of Ekron.

entries.heading: 12. the cry of the city went up to heaven
entries.text: 12. the cry of the city went up to heaven --The disease is attended with acute pain, and it is far from being a rare phenomenon in the Philistian plain [Van De Velde].
